scope: NaturalFPS pipeline optimization, compared with the current support-arm port before optimization
retainedChanges: NaturalFPS naming throughout the game and verification tooling
one transform and palette preparation per frame
cached and revalidated prop child slots
combined opaque prop buckets without distance LOD and with matching instance colors
world shader warmup at the settled light count before presenting the first frame
complete deferred program reflection before first presentation
skip direct-light work for exactly zero-radiance light slots

normalTimingCaveat: The original paired trials below precede the later startup and lighting changes. continuedVerification records the first startup fix; lightingAndReadinessVerification records the lighting benchmarks and the later shared-tree validation separately. All measurements use M4 Pro with other host applications uncontrolled, and do not establish M4 Max performance.

target.reason: The available machine is an M4 Pro. A normal M4 Max browser window remains unmeasured.

measurement.isolation: Sequential browser runs; other host applications are not controlled by this harness.

gpuTiming.caveat: Metal timer queries flush command buffers. These instrumented measurements are excluded from normal frame pacing and from the 60 FPS assessment.

visualParity.review: Combining opaque prop buckets changes their depth-sorting centers. Full-size captures and amplified differences were reviewed. The observed color shifts are not perceptible at normal viewing size; resolution, effects, and geometry are preserved.

validation.skippedReason: The separate million-instance WebGPU timing test requires the dedicated Natural GPU runner.

artifacts: test-results/fps-optimization contains complete benchmark metrics, resource counts, shader data, parity results, and validation logs.

transitions.reference: Same production build with instance substitution, depth collapse and transform reuse bypassed after boot. Prop batching and shader optimizations remain enabled in both variants.

lifecycle.resourceCaveat: Counts track explicit WebGL create/delete calls, not GPU bytes or resources released implicitly when a program or context is destroyed.

sustainedCombat.caveat: One warmed diagnostic run on M4 Pro with other host applications uncontrolled, without GPU queries. This is not an isolated measurement or M4 Max target verification.

continuedVerification.artifacts: test-results/fps-optimization/continued-verification contains all transition PNGs, detailed JSON, combat metrics, and the check log.

warmupFix.cause: The instanced mattress shader was warmed with 3 directional and 21 point lights, but its later draw used 2 and 20. Compile all world layouts once against the HDR target after light visibility settles, before the first frame is presented.
warmupFix.comparisonCaveat: The before and after sustained runs are individual diagnostics on an uncontrolled M4 Pro host, not three paired timing trials.

currentSharedTreeVerification.caveat: Includes the concurrent rifle-grip correction and its current snapshots. Copied tests and snapshots plus a private build prevent later shared edits from changing this run.

lightingAndReadinessVerification.provenance: The completed 72-trial matrix and 720p comparisons precede a concurrent rifle-grip edit. Isolated validation reconstructs that prior rifle source from its saved source map without reverting the shared edit. Its bundle fingerprint differs, so timing and validation fingerprints are recorded separately. A separate frozen copy of the current shared tree validates the updated arm fixtures.
discardedMixedRuns: The first GPU batch rebuilt shared dist after the rifle changed and is excluded from optimization comparisons.
The first shared-tree E2E attempt saw changing arm code and fixtures. Its failures are superseded by isolated and current-tree runs.
changes: Finish deferred link diagnostics and uniform/attribute reflection for newly warmed world programs before first presentation.
Skip the complete point, spot, and directional direct-light bodies when the uniform radiance is exactly zero. Every nonzero light remains active.
Record existing program-info-log calls separately from shader compile submissions in the benchmark.

measurement.measurement: normal frame pacing, no GPU queries
measurement.isolation: Sequential browser runs; other host applications are not controlled by this harness.

hostObservation.observation: Another browser renderer and GPU process were active alongside a separate test process. Their activity was not controlled by this harness. Process CPU activity does not measure GPU utilization.
hostObservation.interpretation: Absolute frame times cannot establish isolated hardware performance or attribute the larger-window slowdown solely to this game.

rejectedPointRangeExperiment.reason: No frame-pacing improvement over the retained uniform zero-radiance guard.
